core.title: Declare a test URN header in every test file
core.given: Any test file, whatever its kind (unit, acceptance, integration or end-to-end), new or existing, identified by the profile's test-file name patterns, outside the trees the profile marks as never scanned
core.when: it is in the test-file scan scope
core.then: Its leading comment block, above the first line of real code (imports included), carries the test URN, declared with the profile's test-URN binding syntax and matching the profile's test URN shape.
prefer: Add the test URN header above the imports, inside the file's leading comment block, using the profile's test-URN binding syntax; companion fields (acceptance URN, phase, layer) may share the same block.
Bind via the header, keeping the file layout; files covering several acceptances need no rename.
avoid: A URN below the imports or code — it reads as missing.
A URN value that does not match the profile's test URN shape.
Encoding acceptance ids in filenames instead of the header; filenames are never parsed.
unless: Not a test file (source files are the coder convention's business).
In a tree the profile marks as never scanned.
core.why: The test URN is the coverage gate's foundation: without it the gate cannot attribute the test or report coverage, and marks the acceptance uncovered while the test passes. Header, not filename, because wagon-level files cover several acceptances; a filename rule would force renaming the suite.
evidence: The test-URN check reports no missing/invalid URN finding for the test file.
A reviewer sees the test URN, in the profile's shape, in the leading comment block before the first import/code line.
verification: The check parses each in-scope test file's leading comment block, using the stack's comment syntax from the profile, for the test-URN binding and requires a value matching the profile's test URN shape.
The header region ends at the first line of real code, so a URN below the imports is treated as missing.
Identity is never derived from the filename; the header is authoritative.

Scan scope: every test file matching the profile's test-file name patterns, of any test kind and whatever its change state (not only changed ones); trees the profile marks as never scanned are excluded. roots.excluded is one stack-wide list, and the exact exclusion classification stays with the stack's checker, to which the realization defers.
Severity 2; disposition strict — the enforcing runner fails on every finding, with no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

values: test URN below the first code line

fires: A new test file is created without a test URN line in its leading comment block.
An existing, unchanged test file in the scan scope has its URN comment placed below the imports, after the first line of real code.
A test file's leading comment block has a URN field whose value does not match the profile's test URN shape.
A wagon-level test file covering several acceptances is relied on for coverage but has no URN header.
doesNotFire: A non-test source file — that is the coder convention's business.
A test file inside a tree the profile marks as never scanned (vendored or build trees).
A test file whose filename does not encode an acceptance id but whose header carries a valid test URN.

neutralityNotes: The obligation is stack-neutral: the leading comment block, above the first line of real code, carries the test URN, and the header, never the filename, is authoritative. Scope is universal over test files — every file matching the profile's test-file name patterns is in scope, whatever its kind (unit, acceptance, integration, end-to-end) and whatever its change state; the earlier unit_test/acceptance_test role split was dropped because it narrowed Bun's scope, and the general test kind resolves through suffix.test. Vocabulary v3 covers every referenced key: urn.test and urn.binding.test are parametric keys of the urn group (artifact param 'test'), so no keys were proposed. The line-comment marker is a profile value; the concrete header example, the detector/validator/finding ids and the rule alias are realization detail (bunOnly); severity and disposition stay in core:verification; roots.excluded carries only the excluded-tree data, while the checker-owned exact exclusion classification is kept in core:verification, matching the realization's deference. 'Product capability' and the coder/tester convention split are method-level vocabulary, not stack facts, so they remain in the core.
